confirmed.statement: (b) What was assigned is when GPT-4 was available during the participant's own ideation task. The AI Generation Component's 'visibility depended on the participant's assigned experimental condition'. In C_before it 'remained visible throughout the main task'. In C_after the 'Display AI' button 'was enabled once participants had created at least three ideas and clicked 'Save Idea''. The Figure 2 instruction panel adds 'Once the 10 minutes ends, the system will automatically display AI.' The form's what_was_assigned follows Sections 3.3 and 3.4.1, and its C_after arm description records the 10-minute rule, so both unlock rules are on the form.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.3, second paragraph; PDF p. 4, Section 3.4.1; PDF p. 4, Figure 2 instruction panel (image text)

confirmed.statement: (b) The tool served the participant's own work. Participants generated, edited, and submitted their own ideas in the Ideation Component, and AI output was 'displayed in the right-hand area for reference'. All three coded outcomes are computed on each participant's submitted ideas. No condition differs only in whose output is evaluated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3.4.1; PDF p. 5, Sections 3.5.2 to 3.5.4

confirmed.statement: Access, not mandated use: Section 3.3 says C_before participants 'used LLM from the very beginning', but the Table 4 condition line for a C_before participant says 'Participants were tasked to independently generate ideas and optionally use LLM for additional support.' The paper reports no LLM usage rates by arm. The form codes the assigned factor as timing of access, which fits both passages.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.3, second paragraph; PDF p. 16, Table 4

confirmed.statement: (c) The tool is generative AI: 'we adopted OpenAI's GPT-4 API to build the streaming content generation feature', in a web application built with Vue.js and Django and hosted on Heroku, as name_model says.

ai_tool.role open_chat and how_used match the text. There are three default prompts, each asking for four ideas within 50 words. 'We also allowed participants to adjust the predefined prompts or create their own prompts', and one participant 'just rewrote the prompt and saw the new result'. summary: The PDF states twice that the 60 Prolific participants were randomly assigned, 30 per condition and between subjects, to a GPT-4 prototype available from the start of their own ideation task (C_before) or only after independent ideation (C_after), and the form's assignment, arms, ai_tool, and ai_design contrast (treatment C_after, control C_before) all match the text (PDF pp. 1, 3-5, 12, 16; Figures 1 and 2). The two qualifications found do not change the coding: Figure 2 adds a 10-minute automatic unlock that the form's C_after description already records, and Table 4 calls LLM use optional, which fits the form's coding of the assignment as timing of access.
